title: checklist: re-point studio-authoring.draft-publish-lifecycle acceptance[10] — a 422 INVALID_METADATA refusal now writes a denied audit row by design (#28355)
body:
domain:devx#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbX9avDwM2goWd7zimE

Filing gate: ① a stale clause, a QA run clause fail (studio-authoring.draft-publish-lifecycle acceptance[10]) whose red line needs an owner (checklist-test §5, "过期规格").
Business reason: the release checklist reads this item FAIL on every run until the clause is re-pointed, although the product does what #28355 decided. A red that is not a regression trains testers to ignore red.
Reader who acts: the `domain:devx` lane, the `checklist-author` procedure on `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/studio-authoring.json` (revise the clause, bump `revision`, add a `history` row, keep `pnpm check:platform-checklist` green). QA suggestion only: p3.
Duplicate search: `draft-publish-lifecycle` → 527 hits, none a re-point card for acceptance[10]; `protocol-refusal-audit` → no card about the clause.
Batch-of: release-18.3.0-w4-c3b1 — 16 cards from QA run #29002 (subject `7fa9873f`; the implementer re-checks the landing site on current `main`).

## What the clause says and what the product does
- Clause (r10): "A 422 INVALID_METADATA spec refusal and a 404 NO_DRAFT write no row"; verify "no row is expected for a 422 spec refusal".
- Product at `7fa9873f`: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-refusal-audit.ts` (#28355) stamps one `denied` audit row per catalogued refusal at each single-item door (save, publish, rollback, delete). `REFUSAL_AUDIT_CODES` = NOT_OVERRIDABLE, NOT_CREATABLE, INVALID_METADATA, DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE. NO_DRAFT, INVALID_REQUEST and 5xx still write none.

## Measured
1. As admin: `PUT /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe?mode=draft&package=PKG` with a widget carrying a stray key → 422 INVALID_METADATA `widgets.0 [unrecognized_keys]`.
2. `GET /api/v1/meta/dashboard/qa_lifecycle_probe/audit` → a row `{"source":"protocol.saveMetaItem","operation":"save","outcome":"denied","code":"invalid_metadata","actor":"ADMIN_ID",…}`. 2 of 2, two different bodies. A NO_DRAFT 404 writes none, and every row carries the authenticated actor (the rest of the clause holds).

## Wanted
Re-point acceptance[10]: a catalogued refusal (the four codes above) writes one `denied` row carrying the actor and the lower-case code; NO_DRAFT, INVALID_REQUEST and 5xx write none. While there, the item's acceptance[3] could spell the wire code `METADATA_CONFLICT` (the audit row's code is lower-case `metadata_conflict`) and say that a stale If-Match must be sent while a draft row exists (with no draft, the published version answers 409 "current is null").
